How GPU rental on Akash works

  1. 1

    Pick a GPU. Compare models and average prices in the table above.

  2. 2

    Deploy a container. In Akash Console, choose a template or paste a Docker image, then accept a provider's bid.

  3. 3

    Pay for what you use. Billing runs while the deployment runs. Estimate costs with the Usage Pricing Calculator.

  4. 4

    Stop anytime. Close the deployment and billing stops.

On-demand or reserved capacity

On-demand

For experiments, bursts and workloads you scale up and down. Deploy in minutes and pay by the hour.

Reserved

GPU rental FAQ

Can I pay only for the GPU hours I use, with no long-term contract?

Yes. On Akash, on-demand GPU deployments are billed for the time they run, with no long-term contract. Close a deployment and billing stops. Only reserved clusters are quoted for a fixed term.

How are GPU prices on Akash set, and are there hidden fees?

Independent providers bid on each deployment, and you see every bid and choose one before anything runs. Akash's GPU pricing table shows the average price per GPU-hour: recent bids, weighted by each provider's GPU count. The bid you accept is the rate you pay. To estimate CPU, memory and storage alongside the GPU, use the Usage Pricing Calculator.

Are there egress or bandwidth fees?

No. Akash doesn't charge egress or bandwidth fees, so serving an inference endpoint or moving checkpoints and datasets out adds no per-GB charge.

How reliable are GPU providers on Akash, and can I see uptime before I choose?

Yes. When you request quotes in Akash Console, each provider's bid shows its region and uptime stats, so you can compare before you accept. You can also limit a deployment to audited providers. For production workloads, reserved clusters come with SLA-backed uptime.

Can I choose where my AI workloads physically run?

Yes. On Akash, every provider's bid shows its region when you request quotes in Akash Console, so you choose where your workload runs before you accept a bid.

Can I run my own Docker image without managing Kubernetes?

Yes. In Akash Console, pick a template or paste any Docker image, choose a GPU and deploy. The provider runs the container on its own infrastructure, so there's no cluster for you to set up or manage.

Do I need crypto to rent a GPU?

No. Akash Console is a managed service: you pay by credit card in USD, the same as any other cloud. No wallet or crypto needed.

Can I reserve dedicated GPUs or a multi-GPU cluster?

Yes. On Akash, reserved clusters run on dedicated bare metal with NVLink, and InfiniBand for multi-node training, with SLA-backed uptime and custom-quoted terms. Request a quote through the bulk order form.

Which GPU should I choose for LLM inference vs. training?

For training and serving large models, pick a data-center GPU: the B300 (288 GB) and B200 (180 GB) hold the largest models per GPU, the H200 (141 GB) suits long-context inference, and the H100 and A100 (80 GB) cover most fine-tuning and serving. For inference on smaller models, fine-tuning and image generation, the RTX Pro 6000 (96 GB) or an RTX 5090 or 4090 costs less per hour.
